newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria court gives suspected Shi'ite Moslems bail.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria court gives suspected Shi'ite Moslems bail.

text.p: A Nigerian court in northern Sokoto state has granted bail to 15 suspected members of the Shi'ite Moslem Brothers group, witnesses said on Wednesday.
The group is campaigning for imposition of Islamic Sharia law in Africa's most populous nation, although only about half the 100 million people are Moslems, mainly of the Sunni sect.
"The area court judge granted 15 bail because the police could not provide evidence against them", one journalist who was at the court said by telephone from there.
He said the 15 were from a group of 43 brought to court two weeks ago by the police on charges of unlawful assembly, illegal preachings, incitement and disturbance of public peace.
The judge adjourned the case of the rest to January 29.
The 43 persons, detained since they were arrested in December, had pleaded not guilty to the charges.

In September, two policemen and five Shi'ites were killed in northern Nigeria when supporters of the fundamentalist Shi'ite Moslem Brothers group clashed with the police while demanding the release of their arrested leader, Sheikh Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky.
El-Zak-Zaky, a radical preacher, was arrested because of illegal publications and radio broadcasts, the police said. He was also alleged to have imported arms.
